audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls Illaoi "he/him" in tldr, winCon, phases and the trade lines, and Level 3, Levels 4-5, First item and 2+ items are marked Illaoi while carrying Akshan-favoured boilerplate.
audit.why: Illaoi is female. The stage sides are right — Akshan owns 1, 2 and 6, Illaoi owns 3 onward — because Test of Spirit at 3 is the moment she stops being a target you can stand in front of.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed and the four contradicted stages now name what owns them: Test of Spirit's 900 range at 3, its 16s cooldown in the 4-5 window, tentacle healing surviving Youmuu's at first item, and her stacked sustain at two.

audit.why: The spike stages hold: Akshan at 2-3 before Test of Spirit, Akshan at Youmuu's, Leap of Faith (120/95/70) at 6 against Comeuppance (100/85/70), and Illaoi at two items. The content layer carries all four.

audit.whatIsWrong: Harsh Lesson does not appear anywhere on the page — neither layer mentions Illaoi's W at all. The page instead calls her "a slow, immobile melee bruiser" with "no ranged tool to answer", and gives no cooldown for anything (the packet flagged this matchup for having no sequencing advice at all).
audit.why: Harsh Lesson is a leap onto her target on a flat 4s cooldown that also makes nearby Tentacles swing at whoever she hits — she is neither immobile nor short-ranged. Test of Spirit reaches 900, further than Avengerang's 850, so the claim that you out-range her is false from level 3 onward. And Prophet of an Elder God heals Illaoi whenever a Tentacle damages a champion, which is the reason anti-heal belongs in this build and the page never said so.
audit.corrected: Harsh Lesson is now named with its 4s cooldown in the stage text, cooldown block, don'ts and wants.foe; Test of Spirit carries its 16s cooldown and 900 range against your 850 throughout; the tentacle heal is stated with the anti-heal instruction attached; and the 'no ranged tool' claim is narrowed to level 1, where it is actually true.

edits.before: This flips. A 2-item Illaoi with tentacle stacks and sustain becomes a wall of effective HP, and your lethality burst stops chunking her — R (Comeuppance) needs her low to execute, and you can't get her there anymore. Your whole job was to convert the early lead before this point. If the game stretches long, do NOT solo her in or near her field; use W (Going Rogue) to roam off-camo, take side waves, and let your team collapse on her instead of dueling.
edits.after: This flips. A 2-item Illaoi with tentacle stacks becomes a wall of effective HP, and her passive heals her every time a Tentacle lands on a champion — buy anti-heal or your burst just tops her up. R (Comeuppance) needs her low to execute, and you can't get her there anymore. Your whole job was to convert the early lead before this. If the game stretches, do NOT solo her near her field; roam off W camo and let your team collapse on her.

notes: The packet reports 62.5% over 24 games here, which sits oddly against a chart that gives Illaoi four of seven stages — worth a look, but I did not flip anything on a 24-game sample. Illaoi's kit file flags Leap of Faith as untargetable and grounding; Riot's own description mentions neither, only damage and a Tentacle spawn per champion hit, so both were treated as tooltip-parse misfires and nothing was written from them.
